subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The turning effect of a force about a point is called:
questions.explain: Torque = force x perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.

questions.q: A force of 20 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.50 m from a pivot. The torque is:
questions.explain: Torque = Fr = 20 x 0.50 = 10 N m.

questions.q: An object is in rotational equilibrium when:
options: The net torque about any axis is zero
questions.explain: For full equilibrium both the net force and the net torque must be zero.

questions.q: The rotational equivalent of Newton's second law is:
questions.explain: Net torque = moment of inertia x angular acceleration (tau = I x alpha).

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body depends on:
options: Its mass and how that mass is distributed about the axis
questions.explain: Mass further from the axis contributes more to the moment of inertia.

questions.q: Angular momentum of a rotating rigid body is given by:
questions.explain: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular velocity.

questions.q: Angular momentum is conserved when:
questions.explain: With zero net external torque, total angular momentum stays constant.

questions.q: A spinning ice skater pulls in their arms. Their moment of inertia decreases, so their angular velocity:
questions.explain: With angular momentum conserved, reducing I increases omega (L = I x omega constant).

questions.q: The rotational kinetic energy of a rigid body is:
questions.explain: Rotational KE = half x moment of inertia x angular velocity squared.

questions.q: A wheel with I = 2.0 kg m^2 rotates at omega = 3.0 rad/s. Its rotational KE is:
A torque of 6.0 N m acts on a body with moment of inertia 3.0 kg m^2. Its angular acceleration is:
questions.explain: alpha = torque/I = 6.0/3.0 = 2.0 rad/s^2.

questions.q: The angular equivalent of linear velocity v is:
questions.explain: Rotational quantities parallel linear ones: omega for v, alpha for a, torque for force, I for mass.

questions.q: For a point mass m at radius r, the moment of inertia is:
questions.explain: A point mass has I = m r^2 about the axis at distance r.

questions.q: A longer spanner makes it easier to undo a bolt because it:
options: Increases the perpendicular distance, increasing torque for the same force
Reduces the force needed to zero
questions.explain: Greater distance from the pivot gives a larger turning moment for the same applied force.

questions.q: A rolling object has kinetic energy that is:
options: The sum of its translational and rotational kinetic energies
questions.explain: A rolling body has both 0.5mv^2 and 0.5 I omega^2.

questions.q: The relationship between linear speed v and angular speed omega for a wheel of radius r rolling without slipping is:
questions.explain: For rolling without slipping, the contact point is instantaneously at rest and v = omega r.

questions.q: Two forces that are equal, opposite and not in line form a:
options: Couple, producing a pure turning effect
questions.explain: A couple produces rotation with no net linear force.

questions.q: On an angular velocity-time graph, the gradient represents:
questions.explain: Just as for linear motion, the slope of omega vs t is angular acceleration alpha.

questions.q: Compared with a solid disc of the same mass and radius, a hoop (ring) has a moment of inertia that is:
options: Larger, because its mass is farther from the axis
questions.explain: Concentrating mass at the rim increases I, so a hoop resists rotational change more than a disc.

questions.q: Angular displacement for constant angular acceleration uses an equation analogous to:
questions.explain: Rotational kinematics mirrors linear SUVAT: theta = omega0 t + 0.5 alpha t^2.
